cells.tense: You are standing on ground that took work to clear, and you are keeping it that way.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Take one exchange on this road all the way through: say what you're holding steady, and accept what comes back for it.
cells.core:
You can keep what took work to win. On a road where the heading has to be held through resistance, you keep it — the thing that changed has stayed standing because you stayed on it, and nothing slipped while your back was turned. You're not gripping it for show. You're standing where it stands.

What keeps it standing is exchange that runs both directions. When only one direction moves — you giving, nobody handing anything back — walking this road costs more than it should, and you feel it in your feet. Let one exchange go both ways this week: name what you're holding steady, and take what's offered for it. The road is yours either way. It just gets easier to walk when the load is fair.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what took work to win, and it holds.
cells.verb: holding steady what already changed, so it stays standing
cells.place: the road where direction has to be kept through resistance

cells.tense: You are already bracing for the moment this falls apart, so you're holding it tighter every day.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Go once toward something on this road that pulls at you, close enough to see what it is, before you know whether it's safe to want.
cells.core:
On the road where the heading is held through resistance, you're not just holding it — you're braced ahead of time. What started as standing firm has become a squeeze. Everything you won gets gripped so hard that nothing gets to come near it, and the grip works harder than the thing it guards needs.

Bracing is no safer than standing. What the grip is holding off is anything that might move you, and there is more of that here than there is danger. Go once toward something that tugs at you — not to decide anything, just to stand close and see what it is. You can set it down after. Coming back with your heading intact after being drawn a little way tells you the grip was not what kept it standing.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it so hard nothing gets near it.
cells.verb: holding steady what already changed, so it stays standing
cells.place: the road where direction has to be kept through resistance

cells.tense: You were standing in a doorway that has already closed, and you are still standing there.
cells.act: refuse the pull off course, once more
cells.ask: When the next thing pulls you off the heading you chose, don't follow it. That's all — no decision after, no plan.
cells.core:
The heading is still in you — you can feel where it points — and here it isn't being walked. On this road, holding the course through resistance is the entire job, and you've stopped doing it, so the energy that used to go into the next mile pools behind a door that shut. Nothing moves. Some part of you is still back where the change landed.

Big decisions won't restart a standstill; one small refusal will. Somewhere near the edge of this week something will tug you off the heading you already picked — a detour, another person's plan, an easier way. Don't follow it, once, and stop there. If it works, it won't feel like much. A road doesn't restart with a feeling.
cells.sheetLine: The heading is still in you and you've stopped walking it.
cells.verb: holding steady what already changed, so it stays standing
cells.place: the road where direction has to be kept through resistance

cells.tense: You are keeping a direction that other people are travelling on, and your account has you merely along for the ride.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Decide something on this road yourself this week that no one is waiting on, and carry it through before you check with anybody.
cells.core:
The heading is being kept, and by your hand. You hold the course on something that took work to win, and you do it so smoothly that it looks like the road ran that way by itself. In your telling, you've been following. What other people lean on is being supplied, and the supplier has left the premises.

A heading you set yourself is where this began. Choose something on this road nobody is waiting on you for, decide it, and carry it through — same day if you can, without asking first. It will feel like ordinary work. Then let it stand as yours, because it is. You were keeping the course before anyone joined you; you just stopped putting your name on it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the heading and call yourself a passenger.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's preserving here is protecting 'what transformation produced' — I can see the holding, not the harvest it came from, so the cores describe the holding and let the person supply the history. A reader could reasonably say the steadiness isn't calmness but stuckness, and the asks survive that: each one is small, doable whether the read is right or wrong, and teaches something either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about peace or stillness as if I could see it — cut; the cores say what the holding does, not what it feels like to be them.
